rv.q: But for such a starry cast Tamara Harvey’s production has a disappointing lack of sparkle.
But Tamara Harvey’s more pedestrian RSC production is saddled with a tepid and starchy new adaptation from Laura Wade, where characters remark: “How cripplingly banal!”
One of the productions greatest strengths is undoubtedly its visual presentation.

Branagh, reviving the accent of his birthplace and of the Billy plays, is excellent as Lopakhin, the son of a serf who has worked hard to gain everything he has and knows the dangers that come without it.
But unfortunately, this tragicomedy-minus-the-comedy just doesn’t quite hit its stride and instead labours its way through what could otherwise have been a truly mesmerising theatrical event.
Despite Sir Kenneth’s shenanigans, overall, and some good supporting performances

cn.t: The RSC's starry Cherry Orchard disappoints, with critics finding the production lacks sparkle, tempo, and vivacity despite its high-profile cast including Helen Hunt and Kenneth Branagh in his return after 30 years.
